newsitem.title: CANADA: Grain shipment delays may shift land to canola.
newsitem.headline: Grain shipment delays may shift land to canola.

text.p: Sustained delays in moving wheat to export ports this crop year may shift farmers' seeding plans in favor of canola, Agriculture Canada said.

"If (increased wheat shipments) do not occur, exports may be lower and stocks higher than currently projected. Reduced delivery opportunities for wheat would likely result in farmers reducing wheat area and increasing canola and special crop area, compared to our current 1997/98 (Aug/July) projections," Agriculture Canada said in the report.
Canada's grain handling system is so congested 42 ships waited to load at Pacific ports Feb 13 for up to 42 days.
The backlog lead to an emergency meeting of the grain and rail industries in Calgary Feb 13 where Canadian Wheat Board said it would probe the cost viability of shipping grain via the United States.
Ag Canada earlier Monday forecast all wheat exports in crop year 1996/97 (Aug/July) to reach 19.85 million tonnes and ending stocks to reach 9.1 million tonnes.
"Due to transportation problems, the CWB has reported that total shipments of wheat and barley are about 1.5 million tonnes behind target," Ag Canada's report stated.
